method: The planner reads the part of GNU make that decides order: explicit rules written targets: prerequisites, pattern rules with one %, recipe lines that begin with a tab, an inline recipe after a semicolon, order-only prerequisites after a pipe, .PHONY, .DEFAULT_GOAL, and the variable operators =, :=, ::=, ?= and +=. Rule lines are expanded when they are read, which is when make expands them, so a target list or prerequisite list that uses a variable reassigned further down the file keeps the earlier value; recipe lines are expanded with the values the variables hold at the end of the file, because make expands them when the recipe runs. The goal is the name in the goal field, otherwise .DEFAULT_GOAL, otherwise the first rule whose target is neither special nor a pattern. The walk is depth first, left to right: each prerequisite and everything below it is placed before its dependent, every target appears once at its first completion, and order-only prerequisites are visited after the ordinary ones. A prerequisite with no rule of its own is assumed to exist as a file, since a browser cannot stat the filesystem, and is reported separately instead of being dropped. A target whose own rule names prerequisites but no recipe takes the recipe of the first matching pattern rule and keeps its own prerequisites, which is what make's implicit rule search does. The planner refuses an empty field, more than 30,000 characters, a recipe before the first rule, a line that is neither a rule, an assignment nor a tab-indented recipe, a pattern containing more than one %, a rule that mixes pattern and ordinary targets, a goal containing whitespace, a goal with no rule and no matching pattern, a file with no default target, more than 400 rule lines or 600 steps, and any cycle, which make would resolve by dropping a prerequisite. An undefined variable expands to nothing, as in make, and is listed; functions such as $(shell ...) and $(wildcard ...), conditionals, include, target-specific variables and suffix rules are reported as not modelled rather than guessed. Nothing is executed and no file is read from disk.

sources.title: GNU Make manual, section 4.2 "Rule Syntax" - the targets: prerequisites form, the tab-indented recipe and the inline recipe after a semicolon

GNU Make manual, section 10.8 "Implicit Rule Search Algorithm" - how a target with no recipe takes one from a pattern rule, and how a stem fills in the prerequisites
